FMA:10427.name: Body wall
FMA:10427.definition: Subdivision of trunk that consists of those organs that separate the body cavity from the body's exterior; together with the body cavity and its contents, the body wall constitutes the trunk (one of the principal body parts). Examples: There is only one body wall.

FMA:10428.name: Wall of thorax
FMA:10428.definition: Heterogeneous cluster which surrounds thoracic cavity and its content; and which includes the ribcage, muscle group of thoracic wall and costal pleura. Examples: There is only one thoracic wall.

FMA:10458.name: Intervertebral disk of first thoracic vertebra

FMA:10636.name: Costocervical trunk
FMA:10636.definition: Trunk of branch of subclavian artery, each instance of which is an artery that arises from the posterior aspect of some subclavian artery, arches backward, and at the neck of some first rib bifurcates into the trunks of some deep cervical and highest intercostal arteries, thus supplying blood to the structures contained in some first two intercostal spaces, the vertebral column, the muscles of some back, and some deep neck muscles.

FMA:10951.name: Inferior vena cava
FMA:10951.definition: Trunk of systemic vein which is formed by the union of the right common iliac vein and the left common iliac vein and  terminates in  the right atrium.

FMA:11195.name: Segment of neural tree organ
FMA:11195.definition: Cell part cluster which is regional part of neural tree organ. Examples: nerve, nerve trunk, ganglion.

FMA:11336.name: Linea alba
FMA:11336.definition: Anatomical junction between aponeuroses of the anterior abdominal muscles.

FMA:11337.name: Zone of continuity
FMA:11337.definition: Zone of connectivity where there is no bona fide boundary between some parts of two contiguous structures.

FMA:11359.name: Cavity of right atrium
FMA:11359.definition: Cavity of atrium which is surrounded by the wall of right atrium and is continuous with the lumen of superior vena cava and inferior vena cava.

FMA:11782.name: Branch of subcostal nerve to external oblique

FMA:12224.name: Segment of tracheobronchial tree
FMA:12224.definition: Organ segment which is regional part of tracheobronchial tree. Examples: trachea, bronchus, intrapulmoanry part of tracheobronchial tree.

FMA:12236.name: Body compartment subdivision
FMA:12236.definition: Compartment of trunk which is enclosed by a body wall subdivision and is demarcated from another body cavity subdivision by an anatomical structure or a conduit, it contains one or more serous sacs, viscera and other organs; together with the other body cavity subdivisions, it constitutes the body cavity. Examples: thoracic cavity, abdominopelvic cavity, abdominal cavity, pelvic cavity.

FMA:12237.name: Organ cavity
FMA:12237.definition: Anatomical cavity, which is surrounded by all morphological parts of an organ; is continuous within the organ; contains one or more body substances. Examples: pericardial cavity, cavity of stomach, cavity of uterus.

FMA:12513.name: Eyeball
FMA:12513.definition: Organ with organ cavity, each instance of which is connected to some optic nerve. Examples: There are only two eyeballs, the right and the left eyeballs.

FMA:12516.name: Tooth
FMA:12516.definition: Organ with cavity, each instance of which has as its parts some dentine, cementum, dental pulp, enamel and cavity. Examples: incisor, molar.

FMA:12845.name: Subcostal vein
FMA:12845.definition:
Venous tree, each instance of which is the vena comitans of some subcostal
artery on the left or right side; it joins some ascending lumbar vein
to form some azygos vein on the right or some hemiazygos vein on the left.

FMA:12861.name: Common basal vein
FMA:12861.definition: Segmental pulmonary vein, each instance of which is a tributary of some inferior pulmonary vein that drains the inferior lobe of some lung.

FMA:12862.name: Superior basal vein
FMA:12862.definition: Segmental pulmonary vein, each instance of which is a tributary of some common basal vein that drains the lateral and anterior segments of the inferior lobe of some lung.

FMA:12863.name: Inferior basal vein
FMA:12863.definition: Segmental pulmonary vein, each instance of which is a tributary of some common basal vein that drains the medial and posterior segments of the inferior lobe of some lung.

FMA:13239.definition: Region of wall of right atrium which is continuous with the wall of right atrioventricular junction.

FMA:13240.name: Wall of outflow part of left atrium
FMA:13240.definition: Region of wall of left atrium which is continuous with the wall of left atrioventricular junction.

FMA:13256.name: Wall of cardiac chamber
FMA:13256.definition: Region of wall of heart which consists of endocardium, myocardium and epicardium that surrounds the cavity of a cardiac chamber.

FMA:13324.name: Cephalic vein
FMA:13324.definition: Tributary of axillary vein, each instance of which is a superficial tributary of vein that arises from the radial side of the dorsal rete of some hand, and winds anteriorly to pass along the anterior border of some brachioradialis muscle; above some elbow it ascends along the lateral border of some biceps muscle and the pectoral border of some deltoid muscle.

FMA:13361.name: Lobe of liver
FMA:13361.definition: Anatomical lobe in liver which is demarcated either by surface landmarks, such as falciform ligament and fissures for ligamentum teres and ligamentum venosum.

FMA:13889.definition: Lobular organ, each instance of which is an epithelial body located at the base of some brain in the sella turcica, attached by a stalk to some hypothalamus, from which it receives an important neural and vascular outflow. It consists of two lobes of differing embryonic origin, the anterior lobe (adenohypophysis), which secretes most of the hormones, and the posterior lobe (neurohypophysis), which stores and releases neurohormones that it receives from the hypothalamus.

FMA:14284.definition: Blood vessel tree organ, the organ parts of which are veins. Examples: There are only three canonical types, systemic venous tree (organ), pulmonary venous tree (organ) and portal venous tree (organ).

FMA:14343.definition: Suprarenal vein, each instance of which is a tributary of some inferior vena cava that drains some right suprarenal gland.

FMA:55268.definition: Organ region, each instance of which has one or more floating fiat boundaries. Examples: apical zone of lung, superior pole of kidney, gingiva, apex of prostate, ascending colon proper.
synonyms: Organ region with floating fiat boundary

FMA:55652.name: Anatomical set
FMA:55652.definition: Material anatomical entity which consists of a maximum number of some instances of discontinuous members of the same class. Examples: set of cranial nerves, ventral branches of aorta, set of mammary arteries, set of thoracic viscera, dentition.

FMA:55661.name: Parenchymatous organ
FMA:55661.definition: Solid organ, each instance of which has as its direct parts instances of some parenchyma and connective tissue stroma. Examples: liver, lung, spleen.

FMA:55662.name: Lobular organ
FMA:55662.definition: Parenchymatous organ the stroma of which subdivides the parenchyma into lobes, segments, lobules and acini. Examples: lung, liver, lactiferous gland, testis.

FMA:55663.name: Corticomedullary organ
FMA:55663.definition: Parenchymatous organ the stroma of which subdivides the parenchyma into cortex and medulla. Examples: thymus, spleen, ovary.

FMA:55665.name: Nonparenchymatous organ
FMA:55665.definition: Solid organ which consists of organ parts that are arranged as fascicles or sheets. Examples: muscle organ, ligament organ, membrane organ, skin, viscerocranial mucosa.

FMA:55670.name: Solid organ
FMA:55670.definition:
Organ the direct parts of which consist of either fascicles or sheets or parenchyma and connective tissue stroma. Examples: Examples: muscle organ, ligament organ, membrane organ, skin, viscerocranial mucosa. 

Old definition:
Organ the unshared parts of which do not surround macroscopic anatomical spaces; only its shared parts (subdivisions of hollow tree organs) contain anatomical spaces. Examples: lung, liver, thymus, ovary, muscle organ, superficial fascia, skin.

FMA:55671.name: Cavitated organ
FMA:55671.definition: Organ, each instance of which has as its direct parts instances of some organ cavity and organ wall. Examples: stomach, urinary bladder, gall bladder.

FMA:55672.name: Organ with organ cavity
FMA:55672.definition: Cavitated organ in which its unshared parts surround one continuous anatomical space. Examples: stomach, urinary bladder, esophagus, uterine tube.

FMA:55673.name: Organ with cavitated organ parts
FMA:55673.definition: Cavitated organ in which its unshared parts surround two or more macroscopic anatomical spaces. Examples: heart, long bone, corpus spongiosum of penis, bulb of vestibule.

FMA:55675.name: Neuraxis
FMA:55675.definition: Organ with organ cavity, each instance of which has as its direct parts some brain and spinal cord.

FMA:55676.name: Segment of brain
FMA:55676.definition: Segment of neuraxis with one or more fixed or anchored fiat boundaries. Examples: thalamus, midbrain, pons, cerebellum, and spinal cord.

FMA:55677.name: Hollow tree organ
FMA:55677.definition: Organ with organ cavity, which consists of an arborizing set of tubular organ parts, the walls of which are continuous and surround a continuous lumen. Examples: systemic arterial tree (organ), tracheobronchial tree, biliary tree.

FMA:55678.name: Male genital duct
FMA:55678.definition: Organ with organ cavity, each intance of which connects some rete testis to some prostatic urethra. Examples: There are only two male genital ducts, the right and the left male genital ducts.

FMA:5897.definition: Immaterial anatomical entity, each instance of which has three spatial dimensions. Examples: body cavity, thoracic cavity, lesser sac, cavity of right atrium, lumen of aorta, mediastinal space, space of anterior compartment of forearm.

FMA:5898.definition: Anatomical cluster in which parts of two or more anatomical structures establish physical continuity with one another or intermingle their component parts. Examples: esophagogastric junction, linea alba, knee joint.

FMA:59495.definition: Zone of hyoid bone, each instance of which is the central part of some hyoid bone.

FMA:61063.definition: Organ with organ cavity, each instance of which connects some vestibule of the conjunctival sac to some nasal cavity. Examples: There are only two lacrimal ducts, the right and the left lacrimal ducts.

FMA:61284.definition: Nonparenchymatous organ which has as its direct parts an aggregate of neurons, the somas of which are located in the neuraxis and their network of neurites (axons) predominantly located outside the neuraxis.

FMA:61412.name: Subdivision of pelvic girdle
FMA:61412.definition: Subdivision of skeletal system of lower limb, each instance of which has as its direct parts some instance of hip bone, obturator membrane, sacro-iliac joint, sacrospinous ligament and sacrotuberous ligament.

FMA:61413.name: Right side of pelvic girdle
FMA:61413.definition: Subdivision of pelvic girdle, each instance of which has as its direct parts some instance of right hip bone, right obturator membrane, right sacro-iliac joint, right sacrospinous ligament and right sacrotuberous ligament.

FMA:61414.name: Left side of pelvic girdle
FMA:61414.definition: Subdivision of pelvic girdle, each instance of which has as its direct parts some instance of left hip bone, left obturator membrane, left sacro-iliac joint, left sacrospinous ligament and left sacrotuberous ligament.

FMA:61680.name: Abdomen proper
FMA:61680.definition: Subdivision of abdomen which is demarcated from the pelvis by the plane of the superior pelvic aperture. Examples: There is only one abdomen proper.

FMA:61681.name: Back of abdomen
FMA:61681.definition: subdivision of back each instance of which has as its constitutional part some complete set of vertebral arches (L1-L5) and anatomical entities located posterior to them; together with back of thorax and back of pelvis constitutes the back. Examples: There is only one back of abdomen.

FMA:61708.name: Subdivision of auriculotemporal part of head

FMA:61731.name: Parietal part of head
FMA:61731.definition: Subdivision of head proper which consists of the parietal bones and all layers superficial to them. Examples: There are only two canonical instances, right and left parietal parts of head.

FMA:61775.name: Physical anatomical entity
FMA:61775.definition: Anatomical entity, each instance of which has three or fewer spatial dimensions. Examples: hemoglobin molecule, mitochondrion, hepatocyte, erythrocyte, heart, head, blood, urine, peritoneal cavity, diaphragmatic surface of heart, inferior margin of liver, apex of lung.

FMA:61815.name: Cardinal segment of brain
FMA:61815.definition: Segment of brain with one or more fixed or anchored fiat boundaries. Examples: thalamus, midbrain, pons, cerebellum, and medulla oblongata.

FMA:61817.name: Cerebral hemisphere
FMA:61817.definition: Segment of telencephalon which has as its direct proper parts cerebral cortex and cerebral medulla.

FMA:61819.name: Left cerebral hemisphere
FMA:61819.definition: Left cerebral hemisphere is one of two bilateral, largely symmetrical organ subdivisions within the telencephalon which contain the cerebral cortex and cerebral white matter.

FMA:61822.name: White matter structure of cerebral hemisphere

FMA:61823.name: Lobe of cerebral hemisphere
FMA:61823.definition: Segment of cerebral hemisphere demarcated by both bonafide landmarks (sulci and fissures) and fiat boundaries.

FMA:61824.name: Frontal lobe
FMA:61824.definition: Frontal lobe is the anterior-most of five lobes of the cerebral hemisphere.  It is bounded by the central sulcus on its posterior border and by the longitudinal cerebral fissure on its medial border.

FMA:61825.name: Temporal lobe
FMA:61825.definition: Temporal lobe is the ventrolateral lobe of five lobes comprising each cerebral hemisphere.  It is bounded dorsally by the lateral fissure and posteriorly by an arbitrary border shared with the occipital lobe.

FMA:61826.name: Parietal lobe
FMA:61826.definition: Parietal lobe is the one of five lobes of the cerebral hemisphere which occupies the dorsal-posterior portion of the hemisphere.  It is bounded by the central sulcus on its anterior border and and by the longitudinal cerebral fissure on its medial border. Posteriorly it shares an arbitrary border with the occipital lobe.

FMA:61833.name: Caudate nucleus
FMA:61833.definition: Nucleus of  brain which is an elongated crescent-shaped mass lying parallel and adjacent to the lateral ventricle throughout its extent.

FMA:61834.name: Putamen
FMA:61834.definition: Nucleus of  brain which lies ventral to the caudate nucleus and internal capsule and medial to the external capsule.

FMA:61835.name: Globus pallidus
FMA:61835.definition: Nucleus of  brain which is located medially to the putamen and laterally to the internal capsule.

FMA:61841.name: Amygdala
FMA:61841.definition: Basal ganglion of telencephalon  which is an almond-shaped gray mass in the dorsomedial part of the temporal lobe.

FMA:61842.name: Septum of telencephalon
FMA:61842.definition: Subdivision of the telencephalon on the midline between the lateral ventricles which contains the septum pellucidum and the septal nuclei.

FMA:61950.name: Internal capsule
FMA:61950.definition: Internal capsule is an organ subdivision of the telencephalon which is made up primarily of myelinated axonal neural tissue (white matter). The internal capsule is a major set of fiber bundles lateral to the thalamus and caudate nucleus and medial to the putamen and globus pallidus. It projects dorsally to the white matter underlying the cerebral cortex.

FMA:61965.name: Fornix of forebrain
FMA:61965.definition: Fornix of neuraxis which connects Ammon's horn of the hippocampus with the mammillary nuclei of the hypothalamus and anterior nuclei of the thalamus.

FMA:61991.name: Trunk of right middle cerebral artery

FMA:61992.name: Forebrain
FMA:61992.definition: Organ component of neuraxis that has as its parts the telencephalon, diencephalon, lateral ventricles and third ventricle. Examples: There is only one forebrain.

FMA:61993.name: Midbrain
FMA:61993.definition: Organ component of neuraxis that has as its parts the tectum, cerebral peduncle, midbrain tegmentum  and cerebral aqueduct. Examples: There is only one midbrain.

FMA:62000.name: Telencephalon
FMA:62000.definition: Organ component of neuraxis that has as its parts the cerebral cortex, cerebral white matter, basal ganglia, septum and fornix, as well as subcortical gray and white matter structures.  There is only one telencephalon.

FMA:62001.name: Diencephalon
FMA:62001.definition: Organ component of neuraxis that has as its parts the epithalamus, thalamus, hypothalamus, subthalamus. There is only one diencephalon.

FMA:62003.name: Metencephalon
FMA:62003.definition: Rostral segment of the hindbrain that has as its parts the pons and the cerebellum.

FMA:62004.name: Medulla oblongata
FMA:62004.definition: Organ component of neuraxis that has as its parts the medullary reticular formation, inferior olivary complex and cochlear nuclear complex, among other structures. Examples: There is only one medulla oblongata.

FMA:62007.name: Thalamus
FMA:62007.definition: Organ component of neuraxis, each instance of which is a large oval mass in the posterior part of some diencephalon adjacent to the lateral wall of some thrid ventricle, containing groups of some nuclei serving as relay centers for sensory impulses and cerebellar and basal nuclear rpojections to some cerebral cortex.

FMA:62008.name: Hypothalamus
FMA:62008.definition: Organ component of neuraxis, each instance of which is the ventral part of some diencephalon, forming the floor and part of the lateral wall of some third ventricle. Anatomically, it includes some preoptic area, optic tract, optic chiasm, mammillary bodies, tuber cinereum, infundibulum, and neurohypophysis, but for physiological purposes the neurohypophysis is considered a distinct structure.

FMA:62023.name: Metathalamus
synonyms: Geniculate group of the dorsal thalamus

FMA:62032.name: Habenula
FMA:62032.definition: Habenula is a segment of the epithalamus that has as its parts the lateral and medial habenular nuclei and the habenular commissure.

FMA:62033.name: Pineal body
FMA:62033.definition: Circumventricular organ of neuraxis which is shaped like a pine cone and  attached on the midline near the posterior and habenular commissures of the epithalamus.

FMA:62045.name: Optic chiasm
FMA:62045.definition: Nerve trunk which is continuous with right and left optic nerves and right and left optic tracts.

FMA:62046.name: Optic tract
FMA:62046.definition: Nerve trunk which is continuous with the optic chiasm and the lateral geniculate nucleus.

FMA:62080.name: Stria medullaris of thalamus
FMA:62080.definition: Stria medullaris of thalamus is a slender fiber bundle on the dorsal surface of the diencephalon which terminates posteriorly in the habenular nuclei.

FMA:62379.name: Optic nerve-tract complex
FMA:62379.definition: Cranial nerve-tract complex which has as its parts the right and left retinas, right and left optic nerves, optic chiasm and right and left optic tracts.

FMA:62382.name: Right optic tract
FMA:62382.definition: Optic tract which is continuous with the optic chiasm and the right lateral geniculate nucleus.

FMA:6720.definition: Neural tree organ, each instance of which supplies some sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles.

FMA:67242.name: Gray matter of neuraxis

FMA:67292.name: Right cerebral hemisphere
FMA:67292.definition: The right cerebral hemisphere is one of two bilateral, largely symmetrical organ subdivisions within the telencephalon which contain the cerebral cortex and cerebral white matter.

FMA:67325.name: Occipital lobe
FMA:67325.definition: Occipital lobe is the one of five lobes of the cerebral hemisphere which occupies the posterior-most portion of the hemisphere.  Anteriorly, it shares an arbitrary border with the parietal lobe and temporal lobe.  Medially, it is bounded by the longitudinal cerebral fissure.

FMA:67329.name: Insula
FMA:67329.definition: Lobe of cerebral hemispheere located in the depths of the lateral fissure and is covered by portions of the frontal, parietal and temporal lobes.

FMA:67498.name: Organ
FMA:67498.definition: Anatomical structure, each instance of which has a maximal complement of instances of  two or more types of tissue or one or more types of essential morphologic unit, a predominantly bona fide boundary and intrinsic vasculature and neural network. Examples: liver, lung, kidney, stomach, urinary bladder, gall bladder.

FMA:67504.name: Subdivision of cardinal body part
FMA:67504.definition: anatomical structure, each instance of which is a regional part of some cardinal body part; it has as its constitutional part some subdivision of the integument, such that for each instance of cardinal body part the meronymic sum of its cardinal subdivisions constitutes the instance of cardinal body part. Examples: thorax, perineum, back of neck, forearm, hand, phalanx, nose, auricle of ear, scrotum.

FMA:67536.name: Cardinal tissue part
FMA:67536.definition: Anatomical structure, each instance of which is a subdivision of some tissue demarcated by bonafide or fiat boundaries. Examples: stratum germinativum, lamina of cerebral cortex.

FMA:67552.name: Anatomical cavity
FMA:67552.definition: Anatomical space which contains portions of one or more body substances and is bounded by the internal surface of one maximally connected anatomical structure or two or more adjacent anatomical structures. Examples: nasal cavity, cavity of stomach, pharyngeal recess space, lumen of artery, cavity of serous sac.

FMA:67598.name: Leaf of cardiac valve
FMA:67598.definition: Organ component which is attached to the chorda tendinea and the fibrous rings of tricuspid and mitral valves.

FMA:67619.name: Organ region
FMA:67619.definition: Cardinal organ part, each instance of which is a fiat subdivision of some organ. Examples: lingula of left lung, tail of pancreas, artery, trochanter, nodulus of semilunar valvule, right side of heart, duodenum, fundus of stomach.

FMA:67687.name: Hindbrain
FMA:67687.definition: Organ component of neuraxis that has as its parts the pons, cerebellum and medulla oblongata . Examples: There is only one hindbrain.

FMA:67771.name: Nipple
FMA:67771.definition: Subdivision of breast which consists of skin, connective tissue and smooth muscle bundle, modified sebaceous glands and papillary part of lactiferous duct.

FMA:67930.name: Intercerebral commissure
FMA:67930.definition: Class of unpaired telencephalic white matter structures consisting of fiber pathways which  project across the midsagittal plane and which serve to interconnect telencephalic structures lying within the contralateral cerebral hemisphere.

FMA:67936.name: Left optic tract
FMA:67936.definition: Optic tract which is continuous with the optic chiasm and the left lateral geniculate nucleus.

FMA:67943.name: Pons
FMA:67943.definition: Organ component of neuraxis that has as its parts the pontine tegmentum and basal part of pons. Examples: There is only one pons.

FMA:67944.name: Cerebellum
FMA:67944.definition: Segment of neuraxis that has as its parts the cerebellar cortex, cerebellar nuclear complex and cerebellar white matter. Examples: There is only one cerebellum.

FMA:7088.definition: Organ with cavitated organ parts, each instance of which is continuous with some systemic and pulmonary arterial and venous trees. Examples: There is only one heart.

FMA:7145.name: Membrane organ

Examples: interosseous membrane of forearm, obturator membrane, tympanic membrane, fibrous pericardium, fascia lata, dura mater.

FMA:7148.name: Stomach
FMA:7148.definition: Organ with organ cavity, each instance of which is proximally continuous_with some esophagus; distally continuous_with some duodenum. Examples: There is only one stomach.

FMA:7149.name: Organ system
FMA:7149.definition: Anatomical structure, each instance of which has as its direct parts instances of one or more organ types which are interconnected with one another by zones of continuity. Examples: nervous system, cardiovascular system, alimentary system.

FMA:7155.name: Neck

FMA:7158.name: Respiratory system
FMA:7158.definition:
Anatomical context:
Organ system, each instance of which consists of tubular and cavernous structures related to airflow from some mouth and nose to some lungs and vice-versa.
Functional system which consists of structures involved in respiration (gas exchange).

FMA:7161.name: Cardiovascular system
FMA:7161.definition: Organ system which consists of heart, systemic and pulmonary arterial and trees, and lymphatic and portal venous trees and body substance contained within.

FMA:7163.name: Skin
FMA:7163.definition: Nonparenchymatous organ that consists of the epidermis, dermis and sets of hair and nails and which surrounds the entire body. Subdivisions of the skin surround various body parts; as a whole, the skin constitutes the external layer of the body.  Examples: There is only one skin.

FMA:7166.name: Left side of heart

FMA:9466.name: Cavity of left ventricle
FMA:9466.definition: Cavity of ventricle which is surrounded by the wall of left ventricle and is continuous with the lumen of the aorta.

FMA:9473.name: Outflow part of left ventricle
FMA:9473.definition: Outflow part of ventricle which is continuous with the aorta.

FMA:9484.name: Atrioventricular bundle
FMA:9484.definition: Subdivision of conducting system of heart each instance of which is the trunk of some conducting system of heart from its origin at the atrioventricular node to the point of division into some right and left bundle branches at the superior end of the muscular part of some interventricular septum.

FMA:9486.name: Right branch of atrioventricular bundle
FMA:9486.definition: Subdivision of conducting system of heart which enters the septal myocardium of right ventricle  to reach the anterior papillary muscle and then subendocardially to the apex of the heart.

FMA:9496.name: Fibrous skeleton of heart
FMA:9496.definition: Fibrous connective tissue which attaches the leaf and cusp of cardiac valve to the wall of heart.

FMA:9498.name: Fibrous ring of mitral valve
FMA:9498.definition: left fibrous ring of heart which consists of the anulus proper, the interfilar connective tissue, the left fibrous trigone and the subaortic curtain of left ventricle that attaches the leaflets of mitral valve to the wall of heart.

FMA:9504.name: Fibrous trigone of heart
FMA:9504.definition: Subdivision of fibrous skeleton of heart which connects the posterior cusp of the aortic valve to the leaf of cardiac valve.

FMA:9531.name: Wall of left atrium
FMA:9531.definition: Wall of atrium which is continuous with the wall of pulmonary vein.

FMA:9533.name: Wall of right ventricle
FMA:9533.definition: Wall of ventricle which is continuous with the wall of pulmonary trunk.

FMA:9535.name: Myocardium of right ventricle
FMA:9535.definition: Myocardium of ventricle which is continuous with the tunica media of the pulmonary trunk.

FMA:9536.name: Endocardium of right ventricle
FMA:9536.definition: Endocardium of ventricle which is continuous tricuspid valve, pulmonary valve  and with the tunica intima of the pulmonary trunk.

FMA:9542.name: Posterior wall of left atrium
FMA:9542.definition: Region of wall of left atrium which is continuous with the walls of the superior and inferior pulmonary veins.

FMA:9550.name: Outflow part of right atrium
FMA:9550.definition: Outflow part of atrium which consists of wall and cavity of the outflow part of right atrium and the tricuspid valve.

FMA:9553.name: Anterior wall of right ventricle
FMA:9553.definition: Region of wall of right ventricle which is continuous with the lateral and septal walls of right ventricle.

FMA:9554.name: Lateral wall of right ventricle
FMA:9554.definition: Region of wall of right ventricle which is continuous with the anterior and inferior walls of right ventricle.

FMA:9555.name: Inferior wall of right ventricle
FMA:9555.definition: Region of wall of right ventricle which is continuous with lateral and septal walls of right ventricle.

FMA:9556.name: Wall of left ventricle
FMA:9556.definition: Wall of ventricle which is continuous with the wall of aorta.

FMA:9558.name: Myocardium of left ventricle
FMA:9558.definition: Myocardium of ventricle which is continuous with the tunica media of aorta.

FMA:9559.name: Endocardium of left ventricle
FMA:9559.definition: Endocardium of ventricle which is continuous with mitral valve , aortic valve, atrioventricular septum and the tunica intima of the aorta.

FMA:9560.name: Anterior wall of left ventricle
FMA:9560.definition: Region of wall of left ventricle which consists of the endocardium, basal, mid and apical anterior zones of myocardium of left ventricle and epicardium of anterior wall of left ventricle and is continuous with the lateral and septal walls of left ventricle.

FMA:9561.name: Inferior wall of left ventricle
FMA:9561.definition: Region of wall of left ventricle which consists of the endocardium, basal, mid and apical zones of myocardium of left ventricle and epicardium of  inferior wall of myocardium of left ventricle and is continuous witht the lateral and septal walls of left ventricle..

FMA:9563.name: Lateral wall of left ventricle
FMA:9563.definition: Region of wall of left ventricle which consists of endocardium, basal, mid and apical lateral zones of myocardium of left ventricle and epicardium of lateral wall of left ventricle and is continuous with the anterior and inferior walls of left ventricle.

FMA:9576.name: Thorax
FMA:9576.definition: subdivision of front of trunk, each instance of which has as its constitutional part some complete set of thoracic vertebral bodies (T1-T12) and some ribcage. Examples: There is only one thorax.

FMA:9577.name: Abdomen
FMA:9577.definition: subdivision of front of trunk, each instance of which has as its constitutional part some complete set of lumbar vertebral arches (L1-L5); it is demarcated from the abdomen internally by the superior surface of the diaphragm and externally by the costal margin and from the pelvis by the plane of the superior pelvic aperture; together with the abdomen and pelvis constitutes the trunk. Examples: There is only one abdomen.

FMA:9578.name: Pelvis
FMA:9578.definition: subdivision of front of trunk, each instance of which has as its constitutional part the bony pelvis; it is demarcated from the abdomen by the plane of superior pelvic aperture; together with the thorax and abdomen constitutes the trunk. Examples: There is only one pelvis.

FMA:9579.name: Perineum
FMA:9579.definition: Subdivision of trunk proper, which is demarcated from the pelvis by the inferior surface of the pelvic diaphragm and from the lower limbs by the perineofemoral lines; together with the thorax, and abdomen, it constitutes the trunk proper. Examples: There is only one perineum.

FMA:9597.name: Salivary gland
FMA:9597.definition: Lobular organ the parenchyma of which consists of glandular acini which communicate with oral cavity. Examples: parotid gland, sublingual gland, lingual salivary gland.

FMA:9600.name: Prostate
FMA:9600.definition: Lobular organ the parenchyma of which has as its parts glandular acini which are continuous with the prostatic part of the urethra. Examples: There is only one prostate.

FMA:9603.name: Thyroid gland
FMA:9603.definition: Lobular organ the parenchyma of which consists of ductless, glandular follicles filled with colloid. Examples: thyroid gland proper, accessory thyroid gland, lingual thyroid gland.

FMA:9607.name: Thymus
FMA:9607.definition: Corticomedullary organ, each instance of which is some lymphoid organ consisting of two pyramidal lobes located in some anterior superior mediastinum, anterior to some heart and posterior to some sternum.

FMA:9611.name: Femur
FMA:9611.definition: Long bone, each instance of which articulates with some hip bone, patella and tibia.

FMA:9612.name: Metacarpal bone
FMA:9612.definition: Long bone, each instance of which articulates with some carpal bone and phalanx of finger.

FMA:9616.name: Muscle of head
FMA:9616.definition: Muscle organ which is a part of the head. Examples: masseter, orbicularis oculi.

FMA:9617.name: Muscle of neck
FMA:9617.definition: Muscle organ which is a part of the neck. Examples: platysma, sternocleidomastoid, cricothyroid muscle.

FMA:9619.name: Muscle of thorax
FMA:9619.definition: Muscle organ which is a part of the thorax. Examples: external intercostal muscle, diaphragm.

FMA:9620.name: Muscle of abdomen
FMA:9620.definition: Muscle (organ) which is a part of the abdomen. Examples: external oblique, rectus abdominis.

FMA:9637.name: Portion of tissue
FMA:9637.definition: Anatomical structure, each instance of which has as its parts some cells of predominantly one type with or without intercellular matrix. Examples: portion of epithelium, portion of muscle tissue, portion of connective tissue, portion of neural tissue.

FMA:9640.name: Portion of connective tissue
FMA:9640.definition: Tissue which consists of fibroblasts, osteocytes or chondrocytes and intercellular matrix produced by these cells. Examples: bone (tissue), dense regular elastic tissue, areolar tissue, neuroglia, adipose tissue.

FMA:9649.name: Decussation
FMA:9649.definition: Anatomical junction in which two or more anatomical structures intermingle segments of their component parts. Examples: commissure, raphe

FMA:9657.name: Anatomical line
FMA:9657.definition: Anatomical boundary entity, each instance of which has one spatial dimension. Examples: margin of tongue, posterior border of right lung, inferior margin of liver, arcuate line of hip bone, sulcus terminalis of heart, pancreatic incisure.

FMA:9663.name: Forearm
synonyms: Intermediate segment of free upper limb

FMA:9664.name: Foot
synonyms: Terminal segment of free lower limb

FMA:9666.name: Finger
FMA:9666.definition: Subdivision of the hand demarcated from the hand proper by the skin crease in line with the distal edge of finger webs. Examples: thumb, right middle finger, left little finger.

FMA:9704.name: Ureter
FMA:9704.definition: Organ with organ cavity, each instance of which connects some renal sinus to some urinary bladder. Examples: There are only two ureters, the right and the left ureters.

FMA:9711.name: Maxilla
FMA:9711.definition: Pneumatized bone, each instance of which is a bone of some upper jaw.

FMA:9712.name: Hand
FMA:9712.definition: Distal free upper limb region, each instance of which consists of some carpus, metacarpus and set of digits.
synonyms: Terminal segment of free upper limb

FMA:9721.name: Tendon
FMA:9721.definition: Organ component of muscle which consists of bundles of collagen fibrils (Type I collagen) bound by loose connective tissue.

FMA:9826.name: Mediastinum
FMA:9826.definition: Subdivsion of thoracic compartment which has as its parts the superior mediastinum and inferior mediastinum.

FMA:9903.name: Peripheral nervous system
FMA:9903.definition: Set of neural tree organs directly connected to neuraxis.

FMA:9906.name: Sympathetic nervous system
synonyms: Sympathetic part of autonomic division of nervous system

FMA:9908.name: Peritoneal sac
FMA:9908.definition: Serous sac, which has as parts the peritoneum and the peritoneal cavity. Examples: There is only one peritoneal sac.

FMA:9914.name: Vertebra
FMA:9914.definition: Irregular bone that articulates with other vertebrae, or with one other vertebra and the skull or the sacrum

UBERON:0000002.name: uterine cervix
UBERON:0000002.definition: Lower, narrow portion of the uterus where it joins with the top end of the vagina.

UBERON:0000211.name: ligament
UBERON:0000211.definition: Dense regular connective tissue connecting two or more adjacent skeletal elements or supporting an organ.

UBERON:0000945.name: stomach
UBERON:0000945.definition: An expanded region of the vertebrate alimentary tract that serves as a food storage compartment and digestive organ. A stomach is lined, in whole or in part by a glandular epithelium.

UBERON:0000948.name: heart
UBERON:0000948.definition: A myogenic muscular circulatory organ found in the vertebrate cardiovascular system composed of chambers of cardiac muscle. It is the primary circulatory organ.

UBERON:0000955.name: brain
UBERON:0000955.definition: The brain is the center of the nervous system in all vertebrate, and most invertebrate, animals. Some primitive animals such as jellyfish and starfish have a decentralized nervous system without a brain, while sponges lack any nervous system at all. In vertebrates, the brain is located in the head, protected by the skull and close to the primary sensory apparatus of vision, hearing, balance, taste, and smell[WP].

UBERON:0000996.name: vagina
UBERON:0000996.definition: A fibromuscular tubular tract leading from the uterus to the exterior of the body in female placental mammals and marsupials, or to the cloaca in female birds, monotremes, and some reptiles[WP].

UBERON:0001103.name: diaphragm
UBERON:0001103.definition: A thin musculomebranous barrier that separates the abdominal and thoracic cavities. Often used for breathing control.

UBERON:0001255.name: urinary bladder
UBERON:0001255.definition: Distensible musculomembranous organ situated in the anterior part of the pelvic cavity in which urine collects before excretion[MP].

UBERON:0001264.name: pancreas
UBERON:0001264.definition: An endoderm derived structure that produces precursors of digestive enzymes and blood glucose regulating hormones[GO].

UBERON:0001350.name: coccyx
UBERON:0001350.definition: A collection of caudal vertebrae in the coccygeal region that are fused and part of the bony pelvis.

UBERON:0001439.name: compact bone tissue
UBERON:0001439.definition: The outer layers of solid, hard bone that covers spongy bone; consists of parallel osteons containing mineral deposits and interstitial lamellae.

UBERON:0002030.name: nipple
UBERON:0002030.definition: Projection of skin containing the outlets for 15-20 lactiferous ducts arranged cylindrically around the tip.

UBERON:0002106.name: spleen
UBERON:0002106.definition: The organ that functions to filter blood and to store red corpuscles and platelets.

UBERON:0002107.name: liver
UBERON:0002107.definition: An exocrine gland which secretes bile and functions in metabolism of protein and carbohydrate and fat, synthesizes substances involved in the clotting of the blood, synthesizes vitamin A, detoxifies poisonous substances, stores glycogen, and breaks down worn-out erythrocytes[GO].

UBERON:0002256.name: dorsal horn of spinal cord
UBERON:0002256.definition: The pronounced, dorsolaterally oriented ridge of grey matter in each lateral half of the spinal cord[MP]. the dorsal (more towards the back) grey matter of the spinal cord. It receives several types of sensory information from the body, including light touch, proprioception, and vibration. This information is sent from receptors of the skin, bones, and joints through sensory neurons whose cell bodies lie in the dorsal root ganglion[WP]. The dorsal region of the mature spinal cord contains neurons that process and relay sensory input[GO].
synonyms: dorsal gray column of spinal cord
dorsal gray matter of spinal cord
dorsal grey column of spinal cord
posterior gray column of spinal cord
posterior gray horn of spinal cord
posterior grey column of spinal cord

UBERON:0002257.name: ventral horn of spinal cord
UBERON:0002257.definition: The ventral grey column of the spinal cord[MP]. The neurons of the ventral region of the mature spinal cord participate in motor output[GO].
synonyms: anterior gray column of spinal cord
anterior gray horn of spinal cord
anterior grey column of spinal cord
ventral gray column of spinal cord
ventral gray matter of spinal cord
ventral grey column of spinal cord

UBERON:0002286.name: third ventricle
UBERON:0002286.definition: Part of the ventricular system of the brain, forming a single large cavity in the midline of the diencephalon; it is continuous with the lateral ventricles through the interventricular foramen and the fourth ventricle through the cerebral aqueduct. (Maryann Martone).

UBERON:0002422.name: fourth ventricle
UBERON:0002422.definition: Part of the ventricular system of the brain, forming a single large irregularly shaped cavity located on the midline of the rhombencephalon, between the medulla, pons and the isthmus ventrally and the cerebellum dorsally. It is continuous with the cerebral aqueduct anteriorally and the central canal of the spinal cord posteriorly. It communicates with the subarachnoid space through its lateral and median apertures.

UBERON:0002481.name: bone tissue
UBERON:0002481.definition: Skeletal tissue with a collagen-rich extracellular matrix vascularized, mineralized with hydroxyapatite and typically including osteocytes located in lacunae that communicate with one another by cell processes (in canaliculi). Bone is deposited by osteoblasts.

UBERON:0003690.name: fused sacrum
UBERON:0003690.definition: A collection of sacral vertebrae in the sacral region that are fused and part of the bony pelvis.

UBERON:0003828.name: abdominal segment bone
UBERON:0003828.definition: A bone that is part of an abdominal segment of trunk [Automatically generated definition].
synonyms: abdominal segment of trunk bone organ
bone of abdominal segment of trunk
bone organ of abdominal segment of trunk

UBERON:0004120.name: mesoderm-derived structure
UBERON:0004120.definition: An anatomical structure that develops (entirely or partially) from the mesoderm.

UBERON:0004247.name: bone of dorsum
UBERON:0004247.definition: A bone that is part of the dorsal region of an animal.

UBERON:0005156.name: reproductive structure
UBERON:0005156.definition: Any anatomical structure that is part of the reproductive system.

UBERON:0005813.name: tubercle
UBERON:0005813.definition: A round nodule, small eminence, or warty outgrowth on an anatomical surface, such as bones, skin, or within the lungs (in the case of tuberculosis). They are also found on the leading edge of Humpback Whale's flippers, improving fluid flow over the flipper's surface[WP].

UBERON:0009853.name: body of uterus
UBERON:0009853.definition: The part of the uterus above the isthmus and below the orifices of the uterine tubes.

UBERON:0009912.name: anatomical lobe
UBERON:0009912.definition: A portion of an organ, such as the liver, lung, breast, or brain.

UBERON:0012332.name: broad ligament of uterus
UBERON:0012332.definition: A broad fold of peritoneum that extends from the side of the uterus to the wall of the pelvis.

UBERON:0013758.name: cervical os
UBERON:0013758.definition: One of two openings in the uterine cervix.

UBERON:0013759.name: internal cervical os
UBERON:0013759.definition: Opening of uterine cervix into the body of the uterus.

UBERON:0013760.name: external cervical os
UBERON:0013760.definition: Opening of uterine cervix into the vagina.

UBERON:0013772.name: left nipple
UBERON:0013772.definition: A nipple that is in_the_left_side_of a body proper.

UBERON:0013773.name: right nipple
UBERON:0013773.definition: A nipple that is in_the_right_side_of a body proper.

UBERON:0015212.name: lateral structure
UBERON:0015212.definition: Any structure that is placed on one side of the left-right axis of a bilaterian.

UBERON:0018140.name: mammary lobe
UBERON:0018140.definition: A cluster of mammary gland lobules. In humans this is a distinct lobe and located in the breast region.

UBERON:2001675.name: mesethmoid cornu
UBERON:2001675.definition: Bony projection that extends from the mesethmoid anteriorly. Mesethmoid cornua are paired processes each articulating with its ipsilateral premaxilla and both cornua bounding a median mesethmoid cleft.

UBERON:4100000.name: skeletal element projection
UBERON:4100000.definition: Anatomical projection that is composed of bone or cartilage tissue.
